review_items.description: Read readelf -A / Tag_RISCV_arch on the libdnnl.so.3.14 object that contains address 0xd257e6 and record whether v/Zvfh appear in its target architecture attribute.

Find the benchdnn softmax driver configuration used for softmax_f32_upstream (search tests/benchdnn for the FWD_D f32 softmax case) and record axis_size/inner_size to confirm which gate clause made jit_exp false.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The hot object's build ISA is unknown (metadata build_isa is null; the sampled benchdnn-elf-A attribute string lists rv64i2p1... without v), so the scalar loops might stem from a translation unit built without V rather than from explicit gating alone.
The gate axis_size >= 16 is intentional to avoid vector overhead on very short reductions; the upstream test may legitimately use a short axis where the maintainers consider scalar competitive.

L1 miss rate 0.161% and LLC miss rate 20% on only 8M references against 11.4G cycles show the workload is compute-side, not memory-side, which strengthens rather than weakens the compute-loop attribution.

findings.conclusion: In softmax_f32_upstream, compute_softmax_f32_rvv executes the scalar fallback exp/sum loop (d25a30-d25a54) that calls expf@plt once per element and accumulates sum_exp through a serial fadd chain with a per-iteration stack store; this loop accounts for ~70% of the function's samples (36% d25a38, 20% d25a40, 13% d25a50) because the jit_exp gate (axis_size>=16, inner_size<=8192) keeps the existing RVV exp_sub_sum JIT kernel unreachable for the measured shape.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Softmax is a complete statistical-reduction-plus-transform flow (max, exp, sum, scale) which the elementwise-activation row explicitly excludes to normalization.
A generic zero-v* claim is superseded by the more specific semantic normalization row owning the softmax stages.
sum_exp is part of the full Softmax flow and the widening-reduction row excludes full Softmax to normalization.

findings.reasoning: Profile hotspots concentrate in the non-jit scalar exp/sum loop: d25a38 36%, d25a40 20% (auipc for expf@plt), d25a50 13%, d25a4c 1%. Source shows this loop is the else branch of jit_exp, which is gated off by axis_size>=16 && inner_size<=8192 (exp_jit_min_len=16). The benchmark executes expf@plt per element with a serialized sum_exp dependency that stores to stack each iteration, producing ~70% of the function's samples. A validated RVV JIT kernel (jit_rvv_softmax_f32_exp_sub_sum) exists at c77dc6 in the same binary but is not reached for this shape.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The compiler may have failed to auto-vectorize the max loop for a reason unrelated to dispatch, such as the max_val loop-carried scalar dependency plus branchy compare/select pattern or a missing -march=v on this translation unit; a vector max reduction kernel exists only for f16 (jit_rvv_softmax_f16_reduce_max), not f32.
The max loop is not the dominant cost; d25844 is 15% versus the exp loop's ~70%, so improving only the max stage bounds total gain by Amdahl and does not address the primary scalar exp path.

findings.conclusion: The Stage-1 max reduction in compute_softmax_f32_rvv is always a scalar value-only maximum loop (d25838-d25850; beqz d25844 at 15%) because the f32 softmax path, unlike the f16 path, provides no vector reduce-max kernel; it is a secondary scalar full scan that contributes roughly 15% of the function's samples.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The full softmax flow belongs to normalization; the extrema row owns only the value-only max stage within it.
The max loop maintains only a value, never an index, so arg-extrema with tie contracts does not apply.

findings.reasoning: The disassembly d25838-d25850 is a scalar value-only max reduction: flw fa5, flt.s, beqz (15% at d25844), fmv.s select, addi/bne loop control. It always runs regardless of jit_exp because the f32 path has no JIT/vector reduce-max (only the f16 path has jit_rvv_softmax_f16_reduce_max). It is a contributing, not primary, cost: 15%+ of samples and a second scalar full scan in the softmax pipeline.

asm.reason: Hotspot lives in compiler-generated scalar loops of compute_softmax_f32_rvv (max-reduction d25838-d25850, expf loop d25a30-d25a54); no handwritten .S in this function and no evidence of assembly dominating.
